stories.headline: 6 baby dolphins were born on Cambodia's Mekong River
stories.summary: This calving season brought 6 Irrawaddy dolphin calves, taking the group on a 75-mile stretch of the Mekong to 118. It is the largest population of the species still living in a river.
stories.why: Since 2014, WWF has helped riverside families earn more beyond fishing, which threatens calves.

stories.stat_label: years old, from an ancient seafloor
stories.headline: The 1st amphibian known to live fully at sea was found
stories.summary: No living amphibian survives in the ocean. But 2 near-complete skeletons from China show Gerrothorax maritimus, an armoured, 3-foot bottom-dweller, lived its whole life at sea.
stories.why: Its bony armour sealed its skin, so it could drink seawater and filter salt with its gills.

stories.stat_label: bags of trash he cleared himself
stories.headline: Told to 'go clean it yourself', a New Yorker did
stories.summary: Joshua Service filmed a dumping site under a rail bridge. Commenters dared him to fix it, so he came back with gloves and a rake and filled 10 trash bags in about 2 hours.
stories.why: A local councilmember planned to honour him at the very spot he cleaned.

stories.headline: Islanders crowdfunded a dig and found a lost monastery
stories.summary: Many of Lismore's 170 residents paid for a dig at their church. It revealed a 6th-century monastery with burials, carved crosses and crucibles likely used for gold and silver.
stories.why: It may have rivalled famous Iona, one of Britain's most important early Christian sites.

fun_fact: Irrawaddy dolphins have no beak: their round, blunt heads make them look more like small belugas.
